text:
mia: seeing a bunch of CI applies failing on gpu-pool-resize, looks like statefile lock isn't being released after autoscaler-triggered imports
sameer: ahh, I noticed the autoscaler does a parallel `terraform import` when new nodes come up, race with our gitops apply
mia: exact error: "Error: Remote state is locked by: arn:aws:dynamodb:.../tfstate-locks (ttl expired?)"
infra-bot: Deploy job #412 failed: terraform apply returned exit code 1 - holding lock on statefile. docs: /internal/infra/locking
jules: can someone paste the dynamo item for the key? wondering if TTLs reset on repeated writes
mia: here's what I ran quickly:
```
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name redwood-tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"workspace:gpu-pool"}}' --region us-west-2
```
response shows LeaseHolder = "ci-runner-7" and ExpiresAt = 2051234500
ops-elaine: ExpiresAt is 67s ago, but lock still present and prevents our subsequent apply because the autodeploy uses `-lock=true`
sameer: I think the autoscaler process reacquires a lock without bumping TTL when it retries, producing a flip-flop: controller A writes, then B writes stale ExpiresAt because of clock skew between runners
jules: we saw clock skew earlier on two runners (NTP drift alert last week). Could be related
mia: for now I manually removed the item to unblock, ran `terraform apply` and the cluster reconciled. Not ideal but unblocked prod-ish stuff :thumbsup:
ops-elaine: can you paste the CLI you used to delete? we need a safe runbook
mia: `aws dynamodb delete-item --table-name redwood-tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"workspace:gpu-pool"}}' --region us-west-2`
ops-elaine: marked as emergency workaround in the runbook, adding note: only after verifying ExpiresAt < now and after contacting owners
sameer: long-term fix ideas:
- increase lock TTL to 5m for workspace with autoscaled imports
- make gitops/ci use `-lock=false` for import step and then do a controlled apply (but that removes protection)
- ensure runners sync NTP at startup and before tf ops
- add Dynamo conditional write that bumps TTL only when owner matches
jules: +1 on conditional write. Also suggest adding a preflight that checks for recent lock and aborts the autoscaler import if lock age < 2m
ops-elaine: file a ticket for ops+infra to coordinate, assign to infra-sre. also want a temporary safeguard: have CI backoff and jitter to reduce simultaneous import attempts
mia: created ticket INFRA-8423 with summary: "Statefile lock flip-flop during autoscaler imports" and linked this thread
infra-bot: Link created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-8423 (priority: P2)
sameer: will prototype conditional-write patch tomorrow, will also add the NTP check in the runner image
jules: also schedule a small postmortem in eng-infra sync next week, quick blameless review of design choices
ops-elaine: note for runbook: if manual delete needed, run in maintenance window and notify #oncall
mia: thanks all, keeping an eye on the pool, will post updates in the ticket
ops-elaine: closing loop: autoscaler resumed without stuck imports ~15m after manual unblock, monitoring for 1h
mia: resolved for now, marking thread done :white_check_mark:
